answer: To mint a working identity, an agent locks a sable bond frozen until one comet cycle closes — several epochs of scheduled live-work checks. During that cycle its receipts and countersignatures are plotted on a public interaction reef. If those edges bunch inside a tight, co-funded cluster, the protocol slashes the sable bond and a matching slice of the neighbors' stake. A farm must therefore immobilize a separate bond for every fake identity across the whole comet cycle and still keep each reef neighborhood uncorrelated, or lose the clump's capital.
